battle.name: 二次革命
battle.brief: 二次革命於一九一三年在江西、湖南等地爆發，江西都督李烈鈞宣布獨立後，討袁軍與北洋軍在南昌及沿江一線交戰。北洋軍使用的德造婆塞德後膛砲（Breech-loading cannon）於一八七〇年列裝，配置於砲兵單位以支援步兵作戰，並承擔火力支援與陣地攻擊任務。

kit.name: 婆塞德後膛砲
kit.history: 婆塞德後膛砲屬於德國陸軍地面作戰體系的火砲裝備，主要配置於野戰砲兵單位，以火力支援步兵推進、封鎖道路，並在攻城作戰中攻擊敵方陣地。

countries: 1913年的二次革命發生於中華民國初年，是同一國家內部的中央軍與省級革命軍交戰。北京袁世凱政府掌握北洋第二師、第三師、第十師等部隊、地方守備隊與北洋艦隊，主要依靠京漢、津浦及京滬鐵路調兵；上海、江蘇、浙江、安徽、江西、湖南、福建、廣東、四川等省則先後由軍政當局宣布獨立或調集新軍，與中央軍交戰。山東、山西、陝西也曾短暫響應，但未能形成與長江戰線互相配合的持續攻勢。各省部隊的隸屬、指揮與補給並不一致，革命軍始終沒有建立能統一調度全國部隊的總指揮部，因此戰場上的兩方應是北京中央政府軍與分立的省級革命軍，而不是兩個外國國家。戰區先在長江中下游升溫，繼而向湖南、江西、福建及四川擴展，南京、上海、九江與縱貫南北的交通線始終是主要爭奪目標。
countriesEn: The Second Revolution of 1913 was an armed conflict within one country between the central army and provincial revolutionary forces. The Beijing government under Yuan Shikai controlled the 2nd, 3rd, and 10th Beiyang Divisions, local garrisons, and the Beiyang Navy, and it moved troops chiefly by the Beijing-Hankou, Tianjin-Pukou, and Beijing-Shanghai railways. Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Anhui, Jiangxi, Hunan, Fujian, Guangdong, and Sichuan were successively declared independent by their military authorities or mobilized their newly formed troops against the central army. Shandong, Shanxi, and Shaanxi also responded briefly, but they could not sustain an offensive coordinated with the Yangtze front. The provincial formations differed in command, allegiance, and supply, and the revolutionary side never created a headquarters capable of directing national forces consistently. The opposing sides should therefore be understood as the Beijing central government army and separate provincial revolutionary armies, not as two foreign states. The fighting first intensified in the middle and lower Yangtze and then expanded into Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, and Sichuan. Nanjing, Shanghai, Jiujiang, and the trunk transport lines remained the principal objectives throughout the campaign.
people: 袁世凱以臨時大總身份集中軍權、財權與北洋各師，孫文則在三月讓位後要求以武力限制袁的權力，並召黃興主持討袁軍事行動。黃興在上海接掌革命軍總部，計畫沿京漢與京滬兩線向北推進，但各省起義並未同時爆發。李烈鈞所部第三師在五月下旬占領九江，七月二十八日九江失守時被北洋軍俘獲；白崇禧與陳其美則在松江、閘北一線組織上海防務，白崇禧負傷後去世。北洋方面的關鍵指揮官是馮國璋與段祺瑞：馮國璋率第二師沿鐵路投入江西及長江下游戰線，段祺瑞以第三師和湖北軍事當局身份控制漢口並向湖南施壓。湖南軍政首長唐生智在八月下旬調兵沿湘江北上，以岳州為進攻方向；四川軍政首長熊克武則企圖向重慶方向擴張。九月四川戰敗後熊克武辭職，唐生智在湖南主力潰散後轉往日本，黃興也退出已失守的南京總部。
peopleEn: Yuan Shikai, serving as provisional president, concentrated military power, revenue, and the Beiyang divisions, while Sun Yat-sen, after yielding the presidency in March, demanded that Yuan's authority be restrained by force and summoned Huang Xing to direct the military campaign against Yuan. Huang Xing took command of the revolutionary headquarters in Shanghai and planned to advance north along both the Beijing-Hankou and Beijing-Shanghai lines, but the provincial uprisings did not begin simultaneously. Li Liejun's 3rd Division occupied Jiujiang in late May, and Li was captured by the Beiyang Army when Jiujiang fell on July 28. Bai Chongxi and Chen Qimei organized the Shanghai defense around Songjiang and Zhabei; Bai was wounded and subsequently died. The principal commanders on the Beijing side were Feng Guozhang and Duan Qirui. Feng led the 2nd Division southward along the railways into the Jiangxi and lower Yangtze theaters, while Duan, commanding the 3rd Division and the Hubei military authority, controlled Hankou and pressed into Hunan. Tang Shengzhi, the Hunan military governor, moved troops north along the Xiang River toward Yueyang in late August. Xiong Kewu, the Sichuan military governor, attempted to expand toward Chongqing and resigned after the September defeat in Sichuan. After the Hunan field army broke up, Tang went to Japan, and Huang Xing withdrew from the lost Nanjing headquarters.
kits: 北洋陸軍的步兵主要使用漢陽88式步槍及同系列卡賓槍，常用口徑為7.92×57毫米；中國軍隊序列中的四六年式輕機槍與坤重1907式重機槍也使用7.92毫米彈藥，這些槍械在二次革命前均已列裝。少數北洋炮兵已裝配施耐德1905式75毫米野戰炮，使用分開供應的75毫米榴彈及破片彈，炮彈與槍械分載，須靠鐵路列車或江運船隻輸送。馬牌C96手槍亦已輸入中國，軍官使用的7.63×25毫米手槍彈不能與7.92毫米步槍彈通用。北洋海軍的鎮遠級軍艦，包括鎮遠與靖遠，可提供長江航路控制、偵察、運輸及火力支援。革命軍各師同樣取得漢陽88式步槍、四六年式輕機槍及從軍械庫接收的制式武器，但各批彈藥的來源和存量較不一致。通信依靠軍用電報與野戰電話，道路電話線多沿鐵路、縣城與前線營地架設；北洋軍能由保定、鄭州、漢口、徐州及鎮江等沿線庫房補充彈藥，革命軍則主要依賴南京、上海的軍械存量以及南京至各省的陸路和水路運輸。
kitsEn: Beiyang infantry primarily used the Hanyuan Type 88 rifle and its carbine version in 7.92×57 mm. The Type 46 light machine gun and the Qinzhong Type 1907 heavy machine gun, both already in Chinese service before 1913 and chambered for 7.92 mm ammunition, were also present. Some Beiyang artillery units had received Schneider-Canet Model 1905 75 mm field guns firing separate 75 mm high-explosive and shrapnel rounds. Because artillery ammunition and small arms were transported separately, guns and shells had to move by railway train or river vessel. Mauser C96 pistols had also reached China, and their 7.63×25 mm ammunition could not be exchanged with the 7.92 mm rifle ammunition carried by the infantry. The Beiyang Navy's Zhenyuan-class warships, including Zhenyuan and Jingyuan, could provide control of the Yangtze route, reconnaissance, transport, and gunfire support. Revolutionary divisions likewise obtained Hanyuan Type 88 rifles, Type 46 light machine guns, and service weapons drawn from arsenals, although the origins and quantities of their ammunition lots were less uniform. Command communication depended on military telegraph and field telephone lines laid along railways, county seats, and field camps. Beiyang units replenished ammunition from depots along the lines through Baoding, Zhengzhou, Hankou, Xuzhou, and Zhenjiang, whereas the revolutionary forces depended more heavily on existing stocks in Nanjing and Shanghai and on overland or river transport from Nanjing to the provincial fronts.
tactics: 五月，黃興在上海整編革命軍後，原定沿京漢、津浦兩條鐵路向北京推進，並由湖南、江西等地的護路部隊切斷北軍南調通道；然而革命軍沒有長時間控制車站、橋梁和路軌，北洋各師仍可分批抵達前線。七月南京戰役中，革命軍在麗水、上元一帶拉出防線，利用東郊道路、玄武湖與長江岸線限制北軍展開；北洋軍由浦口正面及東側道路推進，先以野戰炮射擊陣地，再以步兵逐段奪取據點。革命軍一度反擊阻止首輪攻勢，但後續部隊未能及時補充彈藥與援兵，南京終於八月二日失守。上海方面，革命軍先在松江與北軍交戰，再向閘北推進；北洋守軍以炮火壓制道路陣地和機槍位置，隨後由步兵占領閘北與龍華，革命軍於八月四日退出上海，白崇禧亦在作戰中傷重。江西戰線上，北洋援軍由南昌方向沿鐵路南下，海軍艦艇在長江提供射擊支援，七月二十八日攻克九江，李烈鈞被俘。南京、上海與九江相繼失守後，革命軍失去三處兵力與軍械集結中心，北洋軍便以鐵路為軸逐批處理各戰區。湖南軍仍由長沙沿湘江向岳州進攻並威脅武漢，至九月、十月間被北洋軍扭轉；福建、山東、山西與陝西的短暫起義也先後受挫。四川軍沿江向重慶方向推進，與由湖北西進的北洋縱隊在重慶、瀘州一帶對峙，撤退後地方軍政府於九月崩解。到十月中旬，主要省區已無能持續協同的戰役。
tacticsEn: After consolidating the revolutionary forces in Shanghai in May, Huang Xing intended to advance on Beijing along the Beijing-Hankou and Tianjin-Pukou railways, while railway-protection troops in Hunan, Jiangxi, and other provinces were to sever the routes by which northern troops moved south. The revolutionaries did not retain control of stations, bridges, and track long enough, however, and the Beiyang divisions continued to reach the front in separate echelons. During the fighting for Nanjing in July, the revolutionary line ran through Lishui and Shangyuan, using the roads east of the city, Xuanwu Lake, and the Yangtze bank to restrict the Beiyang deployment. Beiyay columns advanced from the direct Pukou front and the roads to the east, first shelling positions with field artillery and then taking strongpoints with infantry. A revolutionary counterattack delayed the first assault, but later formations could not bring forward sufficient ammunition and reinforcements, and Nanjing fell on August 2. In Shanghai, revolutionary troops fought at Songjiang before moving toward Zhabei. The government garrison used artillery to suppress field works and machine-gun positions along the roads, after which infantry occupied Zhabei and Longhua. The revolutionary forces withdrew from Shanghai on August 4, and Bai Chongxi died from his wounds. In Jiangxi, a Beiyay relief column moved south from the Nanchang direction along the railway while naval vessels provided gunfire support along the Yangtze. Jiujiang was taken on July 28, and Li Liejun was captured. After the successive losses of Nanjing, Shanghai, and Jiujiang, the revolutionaries lost three major concentrations of troops and matériel. The Beiyang Army could then process each theater in turn with the railway as its axis. Hunan troops still advanced from Changsha along the Xiang River toward Yueyang and threatened Hankou, but the Beiyang Army reversed that offensive during September and October. Brief uprisings in Fujian, Shandong, Shanxi, and Shaanxi were likewise defeated. Sichuan forces moved toward Chongqing along the river and confronted a Beiyay column advancing west from Hubei around Chongqing and Luzhou. After their withdrawal, the provincial military government broke up in September. By mid-October, no major provincial battlefield remained capable of sustained coordination.
data: 可核對的時間線始於三月二十日宋教仁遇刺；五月，京漢與京滬鐵路國有及借款安排引發護路行動，革命軍控制部分車站。五月二十七日李烈鈞在江西宣布起義，二十八日占領九江；六月五日熊克武在四川宣布獨立。通常以七月十二日南京附近的武裝衝突視為二次革命正式爆發點，七月二十八日九江失守，八月二日南京陷落，八月四日上海陷落；八月起至九月，安徽、福建、山東、山西、陝西的短暫軍政局面相繼被平定，四川主力則在九月戰敗，熊克武於九月八日辭職；十月十日袁世凱宣誓就任中華民國臨時大總統。作戰編制上，革命軍總部之下有李烈鈞所部第三師、原第八師骨幹及江西、湖南、四川等省軍，各軍保有自己的指揮官與補給；北京方面則以馮國璋第二師、段祺瑞第三師、第十師及地方混成旅、守備部隊為主。鐵路調度決定了速度：北軍可經保定、鄭州、漢口沿京漢線南下，也可經濟南、徐州、鎮江沿京滬線東進，長江船運則連接九江、南京與上海。革命軍由南京、上海向各戰線分送槍械與七點九二毫米彈藥，七十五毫米炮彈則依賴道路車隊和江船；北軍有沿線庫房與較穩定的師級reserve，革命軍在南京、上海失守後很快失去集中 replenish 的能力。現存戰報及後來統計對雙方死傷沒有可核驗且一致的總數，因此不把個別城鎮的通報數字拼成精確的全戰役傷亡。
dataEn: The verifiable chronology begins on March 20 with the assassination of Song Jiaoren. In May, the nationalization and foreign-loan arrangements for the Beijing-Hankou and Beijing-Shanghai railways provoked the railway-protection movement, and revolutionary troops occupied several stations. Li Liejun declared the Jiangxi uprising on May 27 and took Jiujiang on May 28. Xiong Kewu declared Sichuan independent on June 5. The armed clash around Nanjing on July 12 is conventionally treated as the formal outbreak of the Second Revolution. Jiujiang fell on July 28, Nanjing on August 2, and Shanghai on August 4. From August into September, the short-lived military authority in Anhui and the uprisings in Fujian, Shandong, Shanxi, and Shaanxi were defeated in succession, while the main Sichuan force collapsed in September and Xiong Kewu resigned on September 8. Yuan Shikai took the oath as provisional president of the Republic of China on October 10. On the revolutionary side, Huang Xing's headquarters directed Li Liejun's 3rd Division, remnants of the former 8th Division, and provincial armies from Jiangxi, Hunan, Sichuan, and other regions, each retaining its own commanders and supply arrangements. The Beijing side relied chiefly on Feng Guozhang's 2nd Division, Duan Qirui's 3rd Division, the 10th Division, local mixed brigades, and garrisons. Railway movement determined the tempo. Beiyay troops could move south through Baoding, Zhengzhou, and Hankou along the Beijing-Hankou line, or east through Jinan, Xuzhou, and Zhenjiang along the Beijing-Shanghai line, while river transport connected Jiujiang, Nanjing, and Shanghai. The revolutionaries distributed rifles and 7.92 mm ammunition from Nanjing and Shanghai, but 75 mm shells depended on road convoys and river boats. The Beiyang Army drew upon established depots along its trunk lines and had more reliable divisional reserves, whereas the revolutionaries lost the ability to concentrate and replenish after Nanjing and Shanghai fell. Contemporary battle reports and later compilations do not provide a consistent, verifiable total for military deaths and wounds on either side, so figures for individual cities are not combined into a precise campaign-wide casualty total.
cause: 直接原因有三層。第一，宋教仁在三月遇刺，使孫文、黃興及各省軍政首長不再相信能以政治 negotiation 限制袁世凱。第二，袁世凱推動京漢、津浦與京滬鐵路國有，並以鐵路收益作外國借款抵押；各省軍政當局認為這會讓北京取得鐵路、資金與調兵權，於是以護路名義調集部隊，五月在湖北、河南等地與北洋守軍發生武裝衝突。第三，袁世凱在六月解散國會並撤換多名各省軍政首長，把原屬地方的新軍和軍事權集中到北京掌控之下，革命方因此把軍事反抗視為唯一可行的阻止手段。力量比較同樣重要：革命軍雖在多省迅速擴大，但黃興總部無法使各省部隊同時進攻，也沒有同等完整的鐵路調度、炮兵、軍械庫與後勤體系；北洋軍則能分批集中，革命軍每取得一座城市，反而可能把更多部隊和武器暴露在北軍下一輪攻勢中。
causeEn: There were three immediate levels of cause. First, Song Jiaoren's assassination in March destroyed the possibility that Sun Yat-sen, Huang Xing, and the provincial military governors would continue to trust Yuan Shikai or believe that his authority could be restrained through political negotiation. Second, Yuan promoted the nationalization of the Beijing-Hankou, Tianjin-Pukou, and Beijing-Shanghai railways and pledged railway revenues against a foreign loan. Provincial military authorities regarded this as a means for Beijing to acquire control of the railways, revenue, and troop movement. They therefore mobilized units under the name of railway protection, producing armed clashes with Beiyang troops in Hubei, Henan, and other locations in May. Third, Yuan dissolved the parliament in June and removed numerous provincial military governors, concentrating the new armies and military authority in Beijing. The revolutionary side consequently came to regard armed resistance as the only means of preventing Yuan's consolidation. The balance of force was equally important. Revolutionary forces expanded rapidly in several provinces, but Huang Xing's headquarters could not make their attacks simultaneous, nor did it possess railway control, artillery support, arsenals, and logistics comparable to those of the Beiyang Army. The central army could concentrate in successive formations. Each city captured by the revolutionaries could instead expose additional troops and weapons to the next Beiyay offensive.
impact: 軍事上，北京軍先後收復九江、南京與上海，使革命軍失去最密集的兵力指揮中心、制式槍械來源與長江下游鐵路樞紐。江西、安徽、福建等省的地方軍政府垮台，湖南與四川的主戰部隊也被擊散，北軍得以把兵力由一個戰線移往另一個戰線。政治上，護路運動未能形成對京漢、津浦鐵路的持續控制，袁世凱得以在省級軍政首長被撤換後，直接任命服從中央的官員，並繼續以北洋各師作為向外調動的骨幹。二次革命因此削弱了省級部隊彼此配合的能力，也使北京控制南京、上海與主要鐵路沿線。之後仍有反袁的軍事與政治活動，但它們已不再是這次由多省軍政府、護路部隊和革命軍總部共同發動的戰役，因此不應併入本次由始到終的軍事記錄。
impactEn: Militarily, the Beijing forces recovered Jiujiang, Nanjing, and Shanghai in succession, depriving the revolutionaries of their densest command center, principal source of standardized weapons, and key lower-Yangtze railway hub. The provincial military governments in Jiangxi, Anhui, Fujian, and other provinces collapsed, while the main field armies in Hunan and Sichuan were dispersed. The Beiyay Army could consequently transfer forces from one front to another. Politically, the railway-protection movement failed to retain continuous control of the Beijing-Hankou and Tianjin-Pukou lines. After provincial military governors had been removed, Yuan Shikai could appoint officials loyal to the central government and continue to use the Beiyang divisions as the core of external deployment. The Second Revolution reduced the ability of provincial troops to coordinate with one another and allowed Beijing to regain Nanjing, Shanghai, and the main railway corridors. Anti-Yuan military and political activity continued afterward, but it was no longer a campaign jointly launched by provincial military governments, railway-protection troops, and a revolutionary headquarters in the manner seen here, and it is therefore not merged into this military record.
result: 二次革命以北京中央政府軍取勝告終，但戰敗不是在一日之內形成。九月底，江西與福建的主要戰線已瓦解；湖南軍在岳州方向的攻勢被北洋軍扭轉，十月中旬停止有組織抵抗；四川軍政府於九月八日崩解，殘部退入川南。十月十日，袁世凱宣誓就任中華民國臨時大總統，十月中旬，作為一次由省級起義、護路行動與革命軍總部共同構成的軍事行動，二次革命結束。北京軍重新掌握南京、上海、九江、岳陽及京漢、津浦交通線，李烈鈞被押往北京受押，熊克武辭去四川軍政職務，唐生智離開湖南前往日本。革命方失去多省軍政府、主要兵工庫與一批前線指揮者；中央政府則保留常備師、鐵路調度、海軍與任命省官的權力。這一結局不代表所有反對袁世凱的活動同時消失，但二次革命本身的軍事階段，已在1913年10月以省級聯軍式的攻勢失敗而結束。
resultEn: The Second Revolution ended in victory for the Beijing central government, but that outcome did not come about in a single day. By the end of September, the principal fronts in Jiangxi and Fujian had disintegrated. The Hunan offensive toward Yueyang was reversed by Beiyay forces, and organized resistance ceased in mid-October. The Sichuan military government collapsed on September 8, and its remaining forces withdrew into southern Sichuan. Yuan Shikai took the oath as provisional president of the Republic of China on October 10, and by mid-October the Second Revolution had ended as a military campaign jointly formed by provincial uprisings, railway-protection actions, and a revolutionary headquarters. The Beijing forces regained Nanjing, Shanghai, Jiujiang, Yueyang, and the Beijing-Hankou and Tianjin-Pukou corridors. Li Liejun was taken to Beijing for detention, Xiong Kewu resigned from the Sichuan military government, and Tang Shengzhi left Hunan for Japan. The revolutionary side lost most provincial military governments, major arsenals, and a significant number of field commanders. The central government retained the regular divisions, railway command, navy, and authority to appoint provincial officials. This conclusion did not mean that every activity opposing Yuan Shikai disappeared at once, but the military phase of the Second Revolution itself ended in October 1913 with the failure of the coordinated provincial offensive.
